sideEffects: Copy link and Download data stay live during the gap between the hydration task and the deferred read, and so do Export SVG, PNG and LaTeX, Cite and the two export options, which the fixer did not name. The gap has a median of 2.3 to 5 ms by trace. This matters only for a press that is already queued when the hydration task ends, or that comes inside the gap; a deliberate press after the page looks ready cannot land there. In a scratch test that pressed Copy link continuously while /tools/rep/?g=C8&k=7 loaded, with no stretching of the task, 5 of 6 runs landed a press 2 to 3 ms after hydration. It copied http://localhost:7410/tools/rep/, which is the default state A2 node 1: the figure still showed that state, with the picker disabled and data-drawn false. The tool announced 'Link copied.'. That press also counts as the reader's action in history.ts, so the link's load that followed was written by replaceState: the bar went from ?g=C8&k=7 to ?z=1&g=C8&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1&w=&k=7&q=ef:1,1. That is the same state in full encoding, against SPEC 7.4 'Nothing is written on load'. A synthetic change event on the frozen picker in the same window was ignored, but it too made the bar get written in full. On the base a press could not land there, because the hydration task itself drew the link's state and moved the button (3001 presses never reached Copy link). Minor: the copied link and data match what was on screen at that instant. Closing the gap needs ToolFrame (cluster shared-a11y) or T12 freezing its share row.

Note, not caused by this branch: T12.spec.ts:1242 times only the hydration task. The branch moves the build of the link's state into a task of its own, 15 to 21 ms long. The representation steps that follow are unchanged code and still reach 40 to 129 ms under load 9 to 13 on both builds. The longest task from hydration to the drawn figure for C8 node 7 had medians of 52.8 and 40.6 ms on the base and 69.3 and 47 on the branch, within the spread between runs. At load 1 neither build showed any long task.

From reading the code, not by test: the new T12 regression test would pass even without the deferred read's generation guard (g === generation). After a popstate load, readLink finds the state already shown and calls activate again on the same state, so the shown state is the same either way. That is minor: a test that could be stronger.

No other side effect found.
